plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning at a price above my value and losing money; if I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since I pay only the second-highest bid regardless of how high I bid (as long as I'm highest), bidding exactly my value maximizes my expected profit without added risk.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I bid exactly my value ($29), I win whenever the second-highest bid is below $29, paying only that second-highest bid, which guarantees non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a high second bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a single round with no repeated learning needed, truthful bidding is optimal.

This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value: bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a bid between my value and my bid, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $45, I will bid $45 to maximize expected profit truthfully.
